review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

12:1.sourceText: Τοιγαροῦν καὶ ἡμεῖς, τοσοῦτον ἔχοντες περικείμενον ἡμῖν νέφος μαρτύρων, ὄγκον ἀποθέμενοι πάντα καὶ τὴν εὐπερίστατον ἁμαρτίαν, δι’ ὑπομονῆς τρέχωμεν τὸν προκείμενον ἡμῖν ἀγῶνα,
12:1.targetText: Therefore, we also having so great a cloud of witnesses set around us, having put off every weight, and the closely besetting sin, may we run the contest that is set before us through endurance,

groups.note: The actual present set/lying-before participle supplies the relative that is set before in English; the auxiliary belongs to that written verbal predicate rather than an independent Greek be verb.

12:2.sourceText: ἀφορῶντες εἰς τὸν τῆς πίστεως ἀρχηγὸν καὶ τελειωτὴν Ἰησοῦν, ὃς ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῷ χαρᾶς ὑπέμεινεν σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας, ἐν δεξιᾷ τε τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ Θεοῦ κεκάθικεν.
12:2.targetText: looking to the Author and Perfecter of the faith—Jesus, who, for the joy set before Him, endured a cross, having despised shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God;

groups.note: The actual ἀντί can express an exchange/in-view-of relation; LSV for preserves the joy relation without deciding here whether the interpretation emphasizes its motivating prospect or an alternative foregone. It is not a claim that a different ordinary for preposition is printed.
The actual perfect sitting predicate κεκάθικεν is rendered simple past sat down; the source retains its perfect form and resulting seated state rather than a written aorist.

12:3.sourceText: ἀναλογίσασθε γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν εἰς ἑαυτὸν ἀντιλογίαν, ἵνα μὴ κάμητε ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν ἐκλυόμενοι.
12:3.targetText: for again consider Him who endured such contradiction from the sinners to Himself, that you may not be wearied in your souls—being faint.

groups.note: The actual ἀναλογίζομαι compound means reckon up/consider carefully; LSV again consider renders that one predicate. It does not print a separate πάλιν again adverb or necessarily a repeated earlier act of considering.

12:4.sourceText: Οὔπω μέχρις αἵματος ἀντικατέστητε πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνταγωνιζόμενοι,
12:4.targetText: You did not yet resist to blood—striving with sin;

groups.note: The actual πρός marks opposition against sin in the struggle; English striving with sin uses with in the adversarial sense, not cooperation.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

12:5.sourceText: καὶ ἐκλέλησθε τῆς παρακλήσεως, ἥτις ὑμῖν ὡς υἱοῖς διαλέγεται Υἱέ μου, μὴ ὀλιγώρει παιδείας Κυρίου, μηδὲ ἐκλύου ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐλεγχόμενος·
12:5.targetText: and you have forgotten the exhortation that speaks fully to you as to sons, “My son, do not despise [the] discipline of [the] LORD, nor be faint, being reproved by Him,

groups.note: The actual διαλέγομαι is the addressing/conversing predicate; LSV speaks fully expands that one source verb, without an independent Greek fully adverb.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the article with discipline; no corresponding Greek article is printed.
English supplies the article with LORD; the actual divine title is anarthrous.

12:6.sourceText: ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ Κύριος παιδεύει, μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται.
12:6.targetText: for whom the LORD loves He disciplines, and He scourges every son whom He receives”;

12:7.sourceText: εἰς παιδείαν ὑπομένετε· ὡς υἱοῖς ὑμῖν προσφέρεται ὁ Θεός· τίς γὰρ υἱὸς ὃν οὐ παιδεύει πατήρ;
12:7.targetText: if you endure discipline, God bears Himself to you as to sons, for who is a son whom a father does not discipline?

groups.note: The actual second-plural endurance form can be read in the for-discipline endurance statement/instruction; English puts it under its different conditional if construction. The actual endurance head remains, without inferring a Greek conditional particle.

The actual middle προσφέρεται concerns dealing/conduct toward the sons; English bears Himself is that idiomatic conduct predicate, not a general rule that middle voice means self-action or a different ordinary carrying verb.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness connective difference: pinned εἰς is the for/unto preposition governing discipline, not the conditional εἰ. LSV if follows the conditional reading; no if particle is fabricated from εἰς.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective difference: LSV has conditional if, while pinned N1904 prints εἰς, for/unto discipline. The forms and resulting construction remain distinct.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

12:8.sourceText: εἰ δὲ χωρίς ἐστε παιδείας, ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασιν πάντες, ἄρα νόθοι καὶ οὐχ υἱοί ἐστε.
12:8.targetText: And if you are apart from discipline, of which all have become partakers, then you are bastards, and not sons.

12:9.sourceText: εἶτα τοὺς μὲν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν πατέρας εἴχομεν παιδευτὰς καὶ ἐνετρεπόμεθα· οὐ πολὺ μᾶλλον ὑποταγησόμεθα τῷ Πατρὶ τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ ζήσομεν;
12:9.targetText: Then, indeed, we have had fathers of our flesh, correctors, and we respected [them]; will we not much rather be subject to the Father of the spirits, and live?

groups.note: The actual fathers whom we had as correctors are the same immediate objects of the coordinated respected predicate. English resumes those real fathers as bracketed them, without a second independently written Greek pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

12:10.sourceText: οἱ μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ὀλίγας ἡμέρας κατὰ τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς ἐπαίδευον, ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ συμφέρον εἰς τὸ μεταλαβεῖν τῆς ἁγιότητος αὐτοῦ.
12:10.targetText: For they, indeed, for a few days, according to what seemed good to them, were disciplining, but He for profit, to be partakers of His separation;

groups.note: The actual article and beneficial/profitable participle designate what benefits; English profit nominalizes that real beneficial content without another Greek profit noun.
The actual μεταλαβεῖν is a sharing/partaking infinitive; English be partakers nominalizes that one written verb, without separate Greek be and partaker-noun heads.

The actual ἁγιότης is holiness as a quality, rendered separation by LSV. It is not an ordinary spatial separation noun, and is distinct from the ἁγιασμός sanctification noun at12:14. This pairing exposes that actual head rather than deciding the full interpretation from an English gloss.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

12:11.sourceText: πᾶσα μὲν παιδεία πρὸς μὲν τὸ παρὸν οὐ δοκεῖ χαρᾶς εἶναι ἀλλὰ λύπης, ὕστερον δὲ καρπὸν εἰρηνικὸν τοῖς δι’ αὐτῆς γεγυμνασμένοις ἀποδίδωσιν δικαιοσύνης.
12:11.targetText: and all discipline for the present, indeed, does not seem to be of joy, but of sorrow, yet afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness to those exercised through it.

groups.note: The actual πρὸς τὸ παρόν is the for-the-present temporal constituent, with a substantival present participle. English present names that time relation without an independent time noun.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness connective difference: pinned N1904 has an initial μὲν marking the discipline topic, whereas LSV and follows the δέ coordination. The second written μὲν later in the temporal phrase supplies indeed.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective difference: LSV and follows an initial δέ reading; pinned N1904 has μὲν here, not a written and/but coordinator.

12:12.sourceText: Διὸ τὰς παρειμένας χεῖρας καὶ τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα ἀνορθώσατε,
12:12.targetText: For this reason, lift up the hanging-down hands and the loosened knees;

12:13.sourceText: καὶ τροχιὰς ὀρθὰς ποιεῖτε τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν, ἵνα μὴ τὸ χωλὸν ἐκτραπῇ, ἰαθῇ δὲ μᾶλλον.
12:13.targetText: and make straight paths for your feet, so that which is lame may not be turned aside, but rather be healed;

groups.note: The actual lame adjective is substantival, the lame part/person. LSV renders it as that which is lame; its relative copula is supplied rather than a written Greek be verb.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

12:14.sourceText: Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων, καὶ τὸν ἁγιασμόν, οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν Κύριον,
12:14.targetText: pursue peace with all, and the separation, apart from which no one will see the LORD,

groups.note: The actual ἁγιασμός is sanctification/holiness, rendered separation by LSV; it is not an ordinary physical-separation lemma, and remains distinct from ἁγιότης at12:10.

12:15.sourceText: ἐπισκοποῦντες μή τις ὑστερῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεοῦ, μή τις ῥίζα πικρίας ἄνω φύουσα ἐνοχλῇ καὶ διὰ ταύτης μιανθῶσιν οἱ πολλοί,
12:15.targetText: observing lest anyone be failing of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up may give trouble, and through this many may be defiled;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

12:16.sourceText: μή τις πόρνος ἢ βέβηλος ὡς Ἠσαῦ, ὃς ἀντὶ βρώσεως μιᾶς ἀπέδετο τὰ πρωτοτόκια ἑαυτοῦ.
12:16.targetText: lest anyone be a fornicator, or a profane person, as Esau, who in exchange for one morsel of food sold his birthright,

groups.note: The actual βρῶσις is eating/food, here a single meal; English morsel of food expands that meal designation without a separately written Greek morsel/bite noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a be predicate in the lest-anyone-fornicator/profane nominal warning; no corresponding Greek be verb is printed here.

12:17.sourceText: ἴστε γὰρ ὅτι καὶ μετέπειτα θέλων κληρονομῆσαι τὴν εὐλογίαν ἀπεδοκιμάσθη, μετανοίας γὰρ τόπον οὐχ εὗρεν, καίπερ μετὰ δακρύων ἐκζητήσας αὐτήν.
12:17.targetText: for you know that also afterward, wishing to inherit the blessing, he was disapproved of, for he did not find a place of conversion, though having sought it with tears.

groups.note: The actual μετάνοια is repentance/change of mind, rendered conversion by LSV.
The actual feminine singular αὐτήν is rendered neutral English it. Both blessing and change-of-mind nouns are feminine in this context, so grammatical gender alone does not decide the referent.

12:18.sourceText: Οὐ γὰρ προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ καὶ κεκαυμένῳ πυρὶ καὶ γνόφῳ καὶ ζόφῳ καὶ θυέλλῃ
12:18.targetText: For you did not come near to the mountain touched and scorched with fire, and to blackness, and darkness, and storm,

groups.note: The actual dative touching/touchable participle supplies the tangible description and destination relation under come near. LSV touched retains this real predicate, while the explicit mountain noun is separately absent from pinned N1904.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness explicitly prints a mountain noun with the tangible description; pinned N1904 has the dative tangible/burning descriptions without a written ὄρει mountain noun here.

12:19.sourceText: καὶ σάλπιγγος ἤχῳ καὶ φωνῇ ῥημάτων, ἧς οἱ ἀκούσαντες παρῃτήσαντο μὴ προστεθῆναι αὐτοῖς λόγον·
12:19.targetText: and a sound of a trumpet, and a voice of sayings, which those having heard begged that a word might not be added to them,

groups.note: The actual passive adding infinitive is the content of the begging; English presents that same content as that a word might be added, without a separately written Greek that conjunction or finite verb.

12:20.sourceText: οὐκ ἔφερον γὰρ τὸ διαστελλόμενον Κἂν θηρίον θίγῃ τοῦ ὄρους, λιθοβοληθήσεται·
12:20.targetText: for they were not bearing that which is commanded, “And if a beast may touch the mountain, it will be stoned, or shot through with an arrow,”

unmappedTarget.text: or shot through with an arrow
unmappedTarget.reason: This longer punishment clause is present in LSV but absent from pinned N1904, which ends the quotation with will be stoned.

12:21.sourceText: καί, οὕτω φοβερὸν ἦν τὸ φανταζόμενον, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν Ἔκφοβός εἰμι καὶ ἔντρομος·
12:21.targetText: and (so terrible was the sight), Moses said, “I am exceedingly fearful, and trembling.”

groups.note: The actual substantival appearing participle denotes what appeared/was seen, rendered sight; the source remains this real appearance predicate, not a different Greek sight noun.
The actual ἔντρομος is an adjective, trembling/terrified, not a separately written τρέμω verb. Its copula is the actual preceding εἰμι shared by the coordinated descriptions.

12:22.sourceText: ἀλλὰ προσεληλύθατε Σιὼν ὄρει καὶ πόλει Θεοῦ ζῶντος, Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ, καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων, πανηγύρει
12:22.targetText: But you came to Mount Zion, and to [the] city of the living God, to the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of messengers,

groups.note: The actual dative Jerusalem is appositional to the city and its heavenly modifier; English repeats to for that same coordinated/appositional destination without a separately printed preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the bracketed article with city; the actual city noun is anarthrous.

sourceMoved.reason: The actual festal-assembly dative πανηγύρει closes N1904 12:22 and is rendered as to the assembly-place at the start of LSV12:23.

12:23.sourceText: καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ Κριτῇ Θεῷ πάντων, καὶ πνεύμασι δικαίων τετελειωμένων,
12:23.targetText: to the assembly-place and Assembly of the Firstborn registered in Heaven, and to God the judge of all, and to spirits of righteous men made perfect,

groups.note: Pinned πρωτοτόκων is genitive plural, the firstborn people, not a singular proper name. LSV capitalization does not change that printed plural into a singular Christ designation.
The actual οὐρανοῖς is plural heavens; English uses collective singular Heaven for that same heavenly domain.

The actual πανήγυρις is a festal gathering/assembly noun in the dative, moved from raw12:22. LSV renders it assembly-place and coordinates it with Assembly here; no separate τόπος place/building noun is written. Its possible attachment as the angels’ festal gathering versus a coordinated gathering is not decided by the English compound alone.

12:24.sourceText: καὶ διαθήκης νέας μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι παρὰ τὸν Ἄβελ.
12:24.targetText: and to a mediator of a new covenant—Jesus, and to blood of sprinkling, speaking better things than that of Abel!

groups.note: The actual κρεῖττον is neuter singular comparative/adverbial better; English better things states the comparative spoken content without a separately printed plural things noun.

The actual accusative article-plus-Abel phrase is the comparison with Abel. LSV that of Abel makes the associated blood/speaking testimony comparison explicit through metonymy, without a separately written second blood noun or an actual Greek genitive Abel. The note does not resolve whether the implicit comparison emphasizes Abel himself, his blood or his testimony.

12:25.sourceText: Βλέπετε μὴ παραιτήσησθε τὸν λαλοῦντα· εἰ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι οὐκ ἐξέφυγον ἐπὶ γῆς παραιτησάμενοι τὸν χρηματίζοντα, πολὺ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τὸν ἀπ’ οὐρανῶν ἀποστρεφόμενοι·
12:25.targetText: Watch out lest you refuse Him who is speaking, for if those did not escape who refused him who was divinely speaking on earth—much less we who turn away from Him who [speaks] from Heaven,

groups.note: The actual opening speaking participle identifies the speaker whom the readers must not refuse. The final from-Heaven person resumes that same speaking object in the immediate contrast, and LSV repeats the real predicate as bracketed speaks. This shares the opening actual speaking identity, not the distinct earthly divine-speaking predicate, and does not invent a second Greek speaking token.
The actual χρηματίζω divine-instruction participle is rendered was divinely speaking; its one predicate contains the divine-communication sense, not a separately written divinely adverb.

The actual πολλῷ μᾶλλον gives much more reason for the no-escape consequence. English much less expresses the converse lack of escape under that negative argument; this is the whole comparative-negative construction, not a lexical μᾶλλον=less rule.

The actual turning-away middle participle governs the person as its object; English turn away from expresses that same rejected-person relation. The second from is English verb valence, while the separately printed ἀπό belongs to from Heaven.

12:26.sourceText: οὗ ἡ φωνὴ τὴν γῆν ἐσάλευσεν τότε, νῦν δὲ ἐπήγγελται λέγων Ἔτι ἅπαξ ἐγὼ σείσω οὐ μόνον τὴν γῆν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν οὐρανόν.
12:26.targetText: whose voice shook the earth then, and now He has promised, saying, “Yet once [more]—I shake not only the earth, but also Heaven”;

groups.note: The actual ἔτι ἅπαξ is yet once/once more; English more expresses the additional-occurrence force of the whole yet-once construction, not an independent second Greek again token.
The actual σείσω is future I will shake; LSV prints the present shake. The same shaking predicate is retained with its tense difference explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

12:27.sourceText: τὸ δὲ Ἔτι ἅπαξ δηλοῖ τὴν τῶν σαλευομένων μετάθεσιν ὡς πεποιημένων, ἵνα μείνῃ τὰ μὴ σαλευόμενα.
12:27.targetText: and this, “Yet once [more],” makes evident the removal of the things shaken, as of things having been made, that the things not shaken may remain;

groups.note: The actual article nominalizes the quoted words Yet once; English this identifies that same quoted expression, not a separate Greek demonstrative τοῦτο.
The actual yet-once expression denotes the further shaking occurrence; English more expresses that whole additive-time construction without a second source again word.

12:28.sourceText: Διὸ βασιλείαν ἀσάλευτον παραλαμβάνοντες ἔχωμεν χάριν, δι’ ἧς λατρεύωμεν εὐαρέστως τῷ Θεῷ, μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ δέους·
12:28.targetText: for this reason, receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, may we have grace, through which we may serve God well-pleasingly, with reverence and fear,

groups.note: The actual ἀσάλευτος is an unshakable adjective modifying kingdom. English that cannot be shaken paraphrases that same property in a relative/passive-capacity form; no finite Greek be/shake verb or δύναμαι modal is invented from the adjective.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

12:29.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον.
12:29.targetText: for our God [is] also a consuming fire.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the main copula between God and the fire noun phrase. The actual consuming participle modifies fire; it is not a written be predicate joining God and fire.
